given.why: Two loans are lent and never returned, and lines 29-35 expect a reminder for each of them.
Both loans are due 2026-03-16 and the clock is set to 2026-03-17, so both are overdue.
The clock is always 10:00Z, which falls on the same date in nearly every timezone, so code that used local time instead of UTC would still pass.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: Each test gets a fresh in-memory database, so neither loan has a reminder before the run.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: The fake's `sent` list must hold exactly two entries, with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn for each loan.
The reminders table must hold exactly one row for each loan.
Each row must have `sent_on` 2026-03-17, which is today, not the due date.
This is B3's Then: the refused loan1 must leave no row, which would fail if the code recorded before asking.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so on the second run loan1 already has today's reminder.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the run.
The third loan is lent on 2026-03-03, so it is due on the run day itself, which tests the boundary between due and overdue.

then.why: On arrays, `toMatchObject` requires the same length, so any second send for loan1, or any send for loan2 or loan3, fails the test.

given.why: The fake is told to refuse loan1 with a reason.
B5 proves that a failed connection comes back as a refusal, the same result B3's test sets up through the fake.

then.why: The reminders table must equal exactly one row, for loan2, so a row for the refused loan1 would fail the test.
The logs must contain an entry whose event is `reminder.failed`.
That same entry must also have level `warn`.
`expect.objectContaining` matches only level and event, so the log's fields, including `loanId`, are never checked; even a `loanId` set to the member's ID would pass.
No assertion looks at the log's fields, so replacing the refusal's reason with a fixed string, or dropping it, would pass.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan2 must still be sent and recorded after loan1 is refused; this only catches the job stopping early if it handles loan1 first, which its earlier due date suggests but the test doesn't pin.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, one of them refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry must exactly equal one with event `reminders.finished`.
The exact match includes level `info`.
`sent: 2` is matched exactly.
`failed: 1` is matched exactly.

given.why: Every test sends a fixed reminder straight through the real client.

then.why: The recorded method must equal `POST`, and the handler only listens for POST anyway.
The handler is bound to NOTIFY_URL/notifications and the recorded path must equal `/notifications`.
The content-type must equal `application/json` exactly, and the body is parsed as JSON.
The body is compared with `toEqual`, so a renamed or missing key would fail.
The template value is matched exactly.
Both the keys and the values inside `data` are matched exactly.
200, 202 and 204 must each come back as accepted.
A 400 must come back as refused, which catches code that only refuses 5xx; 1xx and 3xx answers are not tested.
A network error must come back as `kind: refused`.

then.part: with a reason naming the status
then.why: The reason must contain `400`.

then.part: or saying the API was unreachable
then.why: The reason must contain `unreachable`.
